content:
United ISD is short 22 employees, and the shortage is concentrated exactly where students can least afford it: sixteen of the open jobs are aides for special education students, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

At a special-called meeting on October 14, Associate Superintendent for Human Resources David Canales told trustees the district's campuses are short-staffed in three areas — special education aides, general teacher aides and custodians. Three of the vacancies are teacher aides and three are custodians; the rest are the special education aide jobs, many of them one-to-one positions assigned to individual students.

For now, substitutes are covering many of the openings, especially the one-to-one jobs. But special education is not a plug-and-play assignment: the district's executive director of special education, Claudia Dovalina-Guzman, said substitutes placed in special education classrooms must first earn Crisis Prevention Intervention (CPI) certification — training in de-escalation and in avoiding physical restraint, which she described as a last resort used only as the law allows. The district is also weighing whether to train substitutes to provide hygiene and personal care for special education students, a task now handled by aides; Superintendent Dr. Gerardo Cruz said the Health Services Department would handle that training and families would be notified whenever a trained substitute provides that care.

Bonuses on the table

Cruz told trustees the administration will ask the board to approve retention payments for aides who stay through the end of the school year: $500 for elementary aides who meet the requirements and $650 for secondary aides who commit to the job. Because the salaries of the vacant positions are already in the budget, Cruz said the payments would not increase spending. The board's next regular meeting is scheduled for Wednesday, October 21.

The district also plans a job fair aimed specifically at special education hires on October 28 — the site and hours had not been set as of the meeting. Canales said the fair is limited to special education because those workers have become the hardest to recruit. State rules requiring 48 or more college credit hours for some instructional aide jobs, with alternative routes to qualify, may also be narrowing the pool: Trustee Dianelle Martinez asked whether the district's education requirements for special education aides are worsening the shortage, and raised the fact that substitutes may earn more than aides despite having fewer duties. Trustee Michelle Molina pointed to the physical strain of the work — including biting and hitting — and suggested pay tiers based on how demanding each assignment is, plus keeping protective gear on hand.

Why it matters

For a special education student assigned a one-to-one aide, that aide is not interchangeable staff — the aide is how the student accesses the classroom. A rotating cast of substitutes, however well trained, is not the same thing. Webb Watch will be watching Wednesday's meeting to see whether trustees approve the retention payments, and the October 28 job fair to see whether the district can close a gap that has now reached 22 positions.

Update — October 26, 2026

The October 28 special education job fair now has a set time and place: KGNS reports it will run from 4 to 6 p.m. on Wednesday, October 28, at the Bill Johnson Student Activity Center, Room 2, 5208 Santa Claudia Lane. At the October 14 workshop, no site or hour had been set. No public reporting found in this check confirms whether trustees approved the proposed $500 elementary and $650 secondary aide retention payments at the October 21 regular board meeting; the payments remain described as a proposal awaiting board action.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times reporting on United ISD's Oct. 14, 2026 special-called board meeting (district staffing update, retention payments and Oct. 28 job fair), Oct. 2026; United ISD Board of Trustees meeting calendar, 2026-2027; KGNS, "UISD to host special education job fair," Oct. 22, 2026.

title: United ISD Is Short 16 Special Education Aides. Its Answer: Bonuses and a Job Fair.
